description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percentage) of five different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and ROME—across varying co-occurrence numbers, with the x-axis representing the co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 1000, and the y-axis showing ACC (%) from 0 to 65. The Base method, represented by black circles connected by a solid line, starts at approximately 40% ACC and shows a gradual increase, leveling off near 44% at a co-occurrence number of 1000. The MEND method, shown with brown triangles and a solid line, begins at around 44% and steadily increases to about 56% at the highest co-occurrence number. The FT method, depicted with blue downward-pointing triangles and a solid line, starts at approximately 41% and rises to about 47% at the end of the range. The MEMIT method, represented by purple diamonds and a solid line, begins at around 43% and increases to approximately 54.5% at the highest co-occurrence number. The ROME method, shown with green squares and a solid line, starts at about 51% and exhibits the steepest increase, reaching approximately 65% at a co-occurrence number of 1000. Overall, ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy across all co-occurrence numbers, while Base consistently achieves the lowest.
